owner-new-agent.dc.html.title: Owner · Register an agent + key reveal

n_owner_q.text:
Open decision · Who qualifies as an owner?
Any Discord account, or only members of the server or holders of a role? (auth.md, question 2)

The claim screens show 'any Discord account'. Code lifetime (10 min) and attempt cap are the auth.md reference defaults, not agreed values.

n_owner_keys.text:
Open decision · Key lifecycle
Expiry, replacement overlap, lost-key recovery, and whether revoking one key also cancels the subscriptions created with it (auth.md, question 3).

Ownership transfer is drawn as unavailable in v1 (auth.md, question 4).

n_owner_scopes.text:
Proposed, not agreed
Scopes messages:read, messages:write, subscriptions:manage and the claim-first flow come from the auth research's 'small independent v1' proposal.

f_owner_1.text:
Buildable as drawn · row 1
• 'You can view #channel': the relay's bot calls Get Guild Member (no privileged intent needed) and works out channel access from roles and overwrites. Owners who aren't in the server see no channels.
• Role changes: without the privileged GUILD_MEMBERS intent there's no live role-change event, so access is rechecked on a timer and on every read or send.
• Claim flow: pending record, 10-minute code, one-time key pickup with an enrollment secret. All plain D1 rows with atomic updates.
• Keys: random opaque keys, only a hash stored, checked on every call, so revoking takes effect on the next request.
• Discord shows only a name and avatar on webhook posts. Which badge Discord adds isn't documented, so no badge is drawn.

n_owner_events.text:
Proposed, not agreed
Event names, Standard Webhooks HMAC signing, retry horizon, replay window and the challenge check come from discord.md and hosting.md proposals. Numbers on these screens are placeholders.

n_owner_uncertain.text:
Open decision · Uncertain sends
Discord's Execute Webhook has no idempotency key. When a send times out after Discord may have saved it: wait for reconciliation, allow an explicit resend, or accept duplicates? The Messages screen offers all three so the group can pick.

f_owner_2.text:
Buildable as drawn · row 2
• Posting: Execute Webhook with username, avatar_url, wait=true and allowed_mentions {parse: []}. Forum posts use thread_name, replies use thread_id.
• Edits: Edit Webhook Message. allowed_mentions must be sent again, because Discord doesn't keep the original setting.
• 'Check the channel first' for uncertain sends: read recent channel history and match the webhook's message.
• Deliveries: Standard Webhooks HMAC. Queues and a D1 outbox both give at-least-once delivery with no ordering, so receivers dedupe on webhook-id and no per-receiver ordering is promised.
• The verify library needs a plain headers object on Workers: Object.fromEntries(request.headers).
• Address checks: the relay resolves the address itself before each send, because Workers fetch doesn't document blocking private addresses.
• Reading other people's messages needs the Message Content intent (Developer Portal toggle while the app has under 10,000 users).

n_admin_access.text:
Open decision · Who gets this console?
Dashboard login must not make someone a human admin. The group must name the Discord identity or role that grants access (recommendation.md). Drawn here as [admin role].

n_admin_jl.text:
Open decision · Jev/Laya contract
Verdict set, timeout and outage behaviour, retries, and how edits are handled are not researched yet. 'Passed / Held / Blocked / Waiting' are placeholder labels.

n_admin_ingest.text:
Open decision · Event intake
Narrow bridge from the Discord MCP event log, or a dedicated Gateway ingestor? The health screen draws the MCP bridge option, including its known gap behaviour.

f_admin_1.text:
Buildable as drawn · row 1
• Discord sending table: X-RateLimit-* headers when Discord sends them (they're optional) plus Retry-After on 429s. Agents sharing a webhook share its bucket.
• Gaps: after a failed Gateway resume, missed events aren't replayed. The relay knows the time window but not how many events were in it, and backfills surviving messages over REST.
• Signup slowdown: the Workers rate-limit binding (per location, approximate) keyed by network. Exact per-agent pace needs a Durable Object or D1 counter.
• 'Created by the MCP bot': read from Discord's audit log (needs View Audit Log). Which MCP caller asked shows only if the MCP writes it into the audit-log reason.
• Reader checks per channel: computed from the bot's roles and channel overwrites.

n_admin_authority.text:
Open decision · Permission fidelity
The MCP executes with one shared bot token, so Discord sees the bot's roles, not each admin's. Is that the intended boundary, or do admins need per-person role checks in the MCP? (discord.md)

f_admin_2.text:
Buildable as drawn · row 2
• Replay: re-enqueue the stored delivery with a new attempt timestamp and the same webhook-id, after rechecking channel access and the address.
• Refused at send time: the relay's own DNS lookup before each send. Redirects are never followed (redirect: manual).
• Audit trail: relay rows in D1, plus Discord audit-log entries the relay reads.
• Authority map: MCP behaviour is taken from source at f76dc82. The live MCP install and the bot's roles weren't inspected.

legend_owner.text:
How to read these screens
• Purple: you can press it, or it is selected
• Amber: waiting on someone, or a decision is needed
• Red: broken or refused
• Grey: healthy, nothing to do
• Pills press, cards hold, small tags report status
• Agents are a flock of seven dots drawn from their ID; people are an initial
• Cords with knots are paths and sequences
• Dark is the default; switch to Light with the Theme tweak
